title: THE CORE-SLOPE TEST -- the registered D2 falsifier (H012) run on the committed X-COP M_encl profiles
registered_kill: H012 D2: cluster inner slope = -1 (NFW) rather than ~-1.5 kills the two-component construction
method: rho_res = d(M_FORW - M_gas - M_star)/dr / (4 pi r^2), per bin on the committed native grid (log-log interpolation of M_encl), OLS log-log fit over the window; MC errors (n=150) from EM_FORW, MGAS_LO/HI, MSTAR_LO/HI, import scatter; cross-checks B (fine-grid OLS) and C (median of local slopes)

honest_limits.HSE_bias: Ettori+19 (the committed R500/M500 source): HSE masses biased ~10-25% vs lensing; radius-dependent part contaminates the slope at the +/-0.1-0.2 level -- comparable to the 0.16 theory-vs-window-NFW gap, small against the 0.5 flat-vs-steep gap
honest_limits.decision_window: this window decides -1 vs -1.5 (7+ sigma) and -1.5 vs -2 (6+ sigma); it CANNOT decide -1.5 vs the window-honest NFW expectation (-1.66, 0.16 apart); the -1 cusp lives at r < ~0.05 R500, below the reliable deprojection

verdicts.V1: median inner slope -1.53 +- 0.25 (scatter), SE 0.074, mean MC error 0.28; per-cluster values in per_cluster; methods agree (A -1.53 / B -1.52 / C -1.60)
verdicts.V2_outcome: ~-1.5 (the theory's value), with the measured median sitting on the registered -1.5 (-0.4 sigma); the flat NFW cusp (-1) and the isothermal r^-2 (-2) are both excluded (>6 sigma); NFW-as-a-model is NOT excluded because over this window its own committed fits predict -1.66 -- the -1-vs-1.5 distinction is undecided at this resolution in the precise sense stated in V3
verdicts.V3_D2_statement: THE D2 FALSIFIER (H012): NOT TRIGGERED ON THE COMMITTED X-COP DATA -- the measured inner residual slope over 0.1-0.5 R500 is -1.53 (median, 12 clusters, scatter 0.25), inconsistent with the kill line -1 at 7.2 sigma and consistent with the theory's registered ~-1.5 at 0.4 sigma; the isothermal r^-2 (the law's one-component profile) is excluded at 6.4 sigma, so the two-component composite (phantom + dust) is required, exactly as H012 constructed it.  THE HONEST CAP: the flat-cusp -1 is only realized for r << rs; the committed NFW fits (median rs = 0.48 R500) predict s = -1.68 over THIS window, only 1.7 sigma from the measurement -- so D2 as registered (NFW -1 vs theory -1.5) is UNDECIDED at this resolution in the decisive direction: both pictures reproduce -1.5 to -1.7 over 0.1-0.5 R500 and both steepen outward.  WHAT RESOLVES IT: the core below ~0.1 R500 (20-70 kpc here) -- lensing inner mass profiles (HST/Subaru strong+weak lensing) that are free of the hydrostatic assumption, or XRISM-class temperature deprojection with non-thermal-pressure corrections; at such radii NFW turns toward -1 while the theory's composite stays ~-1.5.  Until then, the X-COP inner slope stands as a PASS for the theory's registered number (-0.4 sigma) and as a NON-DECISION against NFW.

checks.measured: bins in window: min 34 / max 35 (median 35); grid floor per cluster: 0.021-0.028 R500 (all below 0.1 R500)
checks.reading: the tabulated profiles log-space 30-3000 kpc in 100 points, ~35 bins inside the window; the COVERAGE limit is not the grid (see V3 for the physics limit)

checks.name: V1 [the measured inner slopes with their errors, 12/12 clusters, window 0.1-0.5 R500] s = d ln rho_res/d ln r from the committed M_encl profiles, per cluster, method A with Monte-Carlo errors from EM_FORW/MGAS/MSTAR rows and the import scatter
checks.measured: median -1.53; per-cluster range -2.18..-1.26; scatter 0.25; mean MC sigma 0.28
checks.reading: the primary estimator is the brief's per-bin recipe; methods B (fine-grid OLS) and C (median of local slopes) in the table as cross-checks (sample medians B -1.52, C -1.60)

checks.name: V2a [the flat NFW cusp is EXCLUDED] median inner slope vs -1: the D2 kill line requires the measured slope to be consistent with -1; here it is steeper by 3 sigma or more
checks.measured: median -1.53 vs -1: z = -7.2 (SE 0.07); the point estimate is -0.53 from the flat cusp
checks.reading: the inner residual density is NOT flat: it falls as r^-1.5 ~ r^-1.6 across 0.1-0.5 R500

checks.name: V2b [the isothermal r^-2 profile is EXCLUDED] median inner slope vs -2 (the law's own one-component profile)
checks.reading: the phantom ALONE (r^-2) does not describe the residual in the inner window; the composite (phantom + dust) is required -- matching H012's two-component construction

checks.name: V2c [the theory's registered ~-1.5 is CONSISTENT] median inner slope vs -1.5 within 2 sigma of the measured median
checks.measured: median -1.53 vs -1.5: z = -0.4 (SE 0.07); deviation -0.03; per-cluster values land on both sides (range -2.18..-1.26)
checks.reading: the measured inner slope reproduces the certified residual slope -1.53 (g04a/G008, 75-420 kpc) within the window 0.1-0.5 R500

checks.name: V2d [the honest 4th comparison: the window-honest NFW expectation] the median slope predicted by each cluster's OWN committed M_NFW fit (baryon-subtracted, same pipeline, same window) vs the measured median -- NFW does NOT predict -1 over 0.1-0.5 R500 for realistic cluster rs
checks.measured: measured median -1.53 vs window-honest NFW median -1.68 (scatter 0.18): difference +0.151, combined SE 0.09, z = +1.7
checks.reading: over 0.1-0.5 R500 a genuine NFW (rs ~ 0.3-1.2 R500 from the committed fits) is in its TRANSITION region and predicts s ~ -1.4..-1.9, NOT -1; the data alone therefore cannot separate the theory's -1.5 from NFW on this window -- the flat-cusp -1 reads of NFW are what is excluded, the -1 asymptote lives below, at r ~ 0.02-0.06 R500 (V3)

checks.name: V2e [the radial trend within the window] the measured slope steepens outward (inner-to-outer), with the same sign and scale as each cluster's own committed NFW fit
checks.reading: the residual density steepens toward the outskirts exactly like the committed NFW parametric fits; the innermost sub-window (0.1-0.25 R500) is the flattest part of the measured profile, as both pictures require

checks.name: V3a [the window the data CAN decide] the discriminating budget: the flat cusp (-1) vs the theory (-1.5) differ by 0.5, far above the median SE 0.07 and the statistical scatter; the -1.5 vs window-honest-NFW (-1.66) gap is 0.16, comparable to the systematic budget (HSE bias gradient, [+/-]0.1-0.2)
checks.measured: resolvable at this window: -1 vs -1.5 (z -7.2); NOT resolvable: -1.5 vs -1.66 (z +1.7, combined SE 0.09); HSE bias radius-dependence contaminates the slope at the +/-0.1-0.2 level
checks.reading: the honest conclusion: this window decides steep-vs-flat and excludes r^-2; it cannot decide the theory vs NFW, whose window effective slopes differ by only 0.16

checks.name: V3b [does the current resolution reach the deciding window?] the -1 cusp lives at r < ~0.05 R500 (20-70 kpc here), below the reliable deprojection: the committed native grid starts at 30 kpc (0.02-0.03 R500) but at those radii the X-COP deprojection is model-limited (HSE + spherical + single-phase assumptions, cool cores, sloshing) and the hydrostatic bias (Ettori+19, ~10-25%) has its strongest radial structure there; 0.1 R500 itself sits at only 5-10 PSF widths
checks.measured: NFW asymptote scale r(slope -1.05) = 0.024 R500 vs grid floor 0.021-0.028 R500 and 0.1 R500; HSE bias ~10-25% (committed source Ettori+19), MC slope errors 0.28 mean
checks.reading: COVERAGE reaches 0.1 R500; DECISION power does not reach the -1-vs-1.5 cusp window.  The D2 discriminator needs core data below ~0.1 R500: lensing cores (HST/Subaru strong+weak lensing inner profiles) or non-thermal-pressure-corrected, cool-core-resolved X-ray cores (XRISM-class)
